title: Building your reputation as the expert in your service
audience: Any service operator, including solo operators, starting or growing a business.
learningOutcomes: Set a regular habit of sharing useful, practical content
Turn your experience into content that customers find useful
Direct interested people to a way to contact you or join a list

instruction.heading: People buy from people
instruction.body: Customers hire people they trust. Show your experience and your results. A licensed professional or a specialist operator can build trust by sharing what they actually do.

instruction.heading: Give value most of the time
instruction.body: Most of your content should teach or help, with no ask. Make an offer only occasionally. Useful content includes how-to tips, before-and-after photos with the reasons behind the work, and common mistakes to avoid.

instruction.heading: Choose where your customers look
instruction.body: Use the platforms your customers use: Google Business Profile, Facebook or Instagram for households, LinkedIn for property managers, or local community groups. Post consistently on one or two platforms rather than many.

instruction.heading: Reviews and proof
instruction.body: Ask every customer for a review, not only the satisfied ones. Filtering by mood before inviting reviews can breach platform rules. Do not offer discounts or other rewards in exchange for Google reviews. A link or QR code to the review page makes asking simple. Get the customer's consent before publishing a review, photo or name, and keep a record of it. Privacy law may apply to customer details; whether the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies depends on the business's turnover and activities, so check the OAIC small business guidance. Respond to every review, including negative ones, calmly and factually.

instruction.heading: Capture interest
instruction.body: Give people a next step: a booking link, a short guide or a newsletter. Ask only for the information you need. A newsletter that promotes your business sent by email or text needs the subscriber's consent and a working unsubscribe option under the Spam Act.

procedure: Write three things your customers ask you most often.
Plan one practical post per week that answers one question.
Choose one or two platforms and post on a fixed schedule.
Ask each customer for a review and publish with consent.
Review what gets enquiries and adjust monthly.

workedExamples.situation: A service operator, such as a pool technician, posts a weekly photo of a common algae fix, with the cause and how to prevent it.
workedExamples.reasoning: It teaches something specific and answers a common question, which builds trust without a sales pitch.

commonErrors.prevention: Give value most of the time.

commonErrors.error: Publishing reviews or photos of customers without consent
commonErrors.prevention: Ask first and keep the record of consent.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Check state or territory rules before acting.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: Use the platforms your customers use, and collect consented reviews.
